subject: general
question: Who were the signatories of the Tripartite Treaty signed in 1838 against Dost Muhammad Khan?

options.text: Lord Auckland, Maharaja Ranjit Singh, Shuja ud-Daula
Lord Ellenborough, Maharaja Ranjit Singh, Shuja ud-Daula
Lord Auckland, Maharaja Ranjit Singh, Shah Shuja
Charles Metcalfe, Maharaja Ranjit Singh, Shah Shuja

solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Auckland, Maharaja Ranjit Singh, Shah Shuja**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **signatories of the Tripartite Treaty of 1838 were Lord Auckland, Maharaja Ranjit Singh, and Shah Shuja**.
 
• The treaty** was signed on June 26, 1838 in Lahore.**
 
• **The treaty's main goal was for the parties to help each other in times of need. **
 
• **The treaty stated that Shah Shuja would accept Maharaja Ranjit Singh's suzerainty over Afghanistan. **
 
• **The treaty was signed** during the First Anglo-Afghan War (1838-1842). ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Tripartite Treaty was signed on June 26, 1838 by the British, Maharaja Ranjit Singh, and Shah Shuja**.
 
• The treaty was signed to replace Amir Dost Muhammad as the ruler of Afghanistan with Shah Shuja.
 
• The treaty was signed to stop Russian infiltration into Afghanistan and Persia. 
 
• The British Governor-General, Lord Auckland, wanted to make a treaty with Dost Muhammad, but Dost Muhammad demanded Peshwar. 
 
• Lord Auckland chose Ranjit Singh instead of Dost Muhammad because Peshwar was part of Ranjit Singh's kingdom
